executive_summary.title: Executive Summary
executive_summary.content: Sulfide-based solid electrolytes offer exceptional room-temperature lithium-ion conductivities comparable to liquid electrolytes, but suffer from toxic hydrogen sulfide generation when exposed to moisture [cite_cite_1]. Conversely, oxide-based electrolytes like garnet-structured LLZO demonstrate high chemical stability against metallic lithium and easier air handling, albeit with lower bulk conductivity and higher interfacial resistance which can be mitigated through interlayer engineering [cite_cite_2].

claims.text: Sulfide-based solid electrolytes offer exceptional room-temperature lithium-ion conductivities comparable to liquid electrolytes, but suffer from toxic hydrogen sulfide generation when exposed to moisture.

Oxide-based electrolytes like garnet-structured LLZO demonstrate high chemical stability against metallic lithium and easier air handling, albeit with lower bulk conductivity and higher interfacial resistance which can be mitigated through interlayer engineering.

sections.title: Comparative Performance of Sulfide and Oxide Electrolytes
sections.content: Sulfide-based solid electrolytes such as LGPS and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl exhibit exceptional room-temperature lithium-ion conductivities exceeding 1.2e-2 S/cm [cite_cite_3]. However, a major safety concern is that sulfides react violently with ambient moisture to produce toxic hydrogen sulfide gas [cite_cite_4]. On the other hand, garnet-structured oxide electrolytes like LLZO possess superior chemical stability against metallic lithium [cite_cite_5]. While LLZO exhibits a lower bulk conductivity of 1.0e-3 S/cm and high initial interfacial resistance, modifying the interface with a 5-nanometer amorphous atomic-layer-deposited zinc oxide interlayer successfully reduces the interfacial area-specific resistance from 1200 ohm-cm^2 to 12 ohm-cm^2 [cite_cite_6].

claims.text: Sulfide-based solid electrolytes such as LGPS and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl exhibit exceptional room-temperature lithium-ion conductivities exceeding 1.2e-2 S/cm.

citations.quoted_passage: Sulfide-based solid electrolytes such as Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl exhibit exceptional room-temperature lithium-ion conductivities exceeding 1.2e-2 S/cm

claims.text: Sulfides react violently with ambient moisture to produce toxic hydrogen sulfide (H2S) gas, necessitating strict dry-room assembly.
Garnet-structured oxide electrolytes such as LLZO possess superior chemical stability against metallic lithium and allow air handling.

LLZO exhibits a lower bulk conductivity of 1.0e-3 S/cm, but applying a 5-nanometer amorphous atomic-layer-deposited zinc oxide interlayer reduces interfacial area-specific resistance from 1200 ohm-cm^2 to 12 ohm-cm^2.

conclusion.title: Conclusion and Future Outlook
conclusion.content: Both sulfide and oxide electrolytes present distinct trade-offs for all-solid-state lithium batteries. Sulfides offer superior ionic conductivity at the cost of severe moisture reactivity and safety hazards [cite_cite_7]. Oxides provide enhanced safety and stability with metallic lithium, though engineering solutions like interlayers are required to overcome high interfacial resistance [cite_cite_8].

claims.text: Sulfides offer superior ionic conductivity at the cost of severe moisture reactivity and safety hazards.
Oxides provide enhanced safety and stability with metallic lithium, though engineering solutions like interlayers are required to overcome high interfacial resistance.

limitations: Data is restricted to specific compositions (LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO) without broader coverage of alternative solid electrolyte families.
Long-term cycling durability and scalability of ZnO interlayers remain to be fully evaluated across varying operational parameters.
